tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: A public speaker who rides the L train argued, based on his simulation of MTA trip data, that closing the Third Avenue L stop would save New Yorkers significant travel time because few riders board or alight there. He noted the stop is not a transfer station and is not wheelchair accessible. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about piloting the closure of the Third Avenue stop.

tickets.title: Bike storage and delivery worker conditions on 11th Street
tickets.requester: Keith Powers (Assembly Member); public speaker (unnamed); Board member (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric delivery bikes are stored on sidewalks and streets at 11th Street, obstructing businesses, residents, and pedestrians. Delivery workers have no legal parking or corral space, and enforcement is planned for October 7, which the speakers said would confiscate bikes and burden workers. Action: Work with the precinct and agencies on a compassionate enforcement approach, help find legal storage sites, and provide multilingual notice to workers before enforcement begins.

tickets.title: Drug activity and lighting in Seward Park
tickets.requester: Niles Robinson (Borough President's office liaison); Board member (unnamed); District Manager (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Drug activity and homelessness in Seward Park have increased, and the Seward Park Conservancy and Lower East Side Ecology Center have complained about drug use near their building. Dark areas in the park were also raised as contributing to drug use. Action: Follow up with the Seventh Precinct, have residents report out-of-service park lights through 311, and consider whether mobile crisis teams could expand to address drug use in the park.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and resolutions
tickets.summary: The joint land use and economic development committee met with EDC about the RFP for Essex Market, but EDC could not confirm that the board's resolutions were incorporated. The board passed resolutions asking EDC to postpone issuing the RFP so the community market remains a community market. Action: Ask EDC to postpone the RFP and confirm how the board's resolutions are included, through a follow-up meeting later this week.

tickets.title: Denial recommendation for 11 Allen Street liquor license
tickets.requester: Michelle Cooper Smith (board member); Carlin Chan (community member); Board member (unnamed)
tickets.summary: The board voted 20 yes, 10 no, and 9 abstaining to recommend a straight denial of the August SLA application for 11 Allen Street, the new location of an operator whose former location had problems. The committee had earlier proposed approval with stipulations, and the board noted the applicant could obtain approval without stipulations if the community does not appear at the SLA hearing. Action: Organize community members to attend the SLA hearing to support the denial, and have staff pull 311 complaints tied to the former location.

tickets.title: Clerical corrections to August SLA resolutions for Cozy Cafe and Soft Hours Tea House
tickets.location_raw: Cozy Cafe; Soft Hours Tea House
tickets.requester: Board member (unnamed); Executive committee or SLA committee chair (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Resolution text for August agenda items three (Cozy Cafe) and ten (Soft Hours Tea House) incorrectly referred to full on-premises licenses when the applications were for beer and wine licenses. The clerical errors were identified and noted for correction. Action: None; the board acknowledged the corrections to the beer and wine license language.

tickets.title: Public restroom pilot locations in the district
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms citywide as a one-year DOT pilot, with two planned for the district at Delancey Plaza and Cooper Square at East Sixth Street and Third Avenue. Concerns were raised about access rules and emergency calls. Action: Draft and vote on a resolution next month to set out how the pilot restrooms should operate and be accessed.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits and Canal Street redesign letter
tickets.requester: Transportation committee chair (unnamed); Arnett Scott (transportation committee co-chair)
tickets.summary: The board sent a letter to the mayor and DOT restating community concerns about the foot of the Manhattan Bridge exits, following a recent fatal crash. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign, which has not been updated since January. Action: Await a response from the mayor and DOT and press for the requested Canal Street redesign update.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact on FDR Drive follow-up
tickets.summary: A board member asked whether the congestion pricing impacts projected for FDR Drive actually occurred, noting that MTA and DOT released an air quality report and the board previously passed a resolution on this issue. The member asked whether reporting is planned and, if not, whether it can be requested. Action: Follow up with MTA and DOT on whether projected FDR congestion occurred and request any planned reporting.

tickets.title: Transportation equity analysis with IBO
tickets.requester: Transportation committee chair (unnamed); Susan (District Manager staff)
tickets.summary: The transportation committee met with the Independent Budget Office to assess whether District 3 receives equitable transportation resources compared with other districts. About ten ideas were narrowed to three, including cross-town buses and neighborhood parking locations. Action: Ask IBO to research the shortlisted transportation equity ideas, including cross-town buses and neighborhood parking locations.

tickets.title: Vision Zero intersection inclusion request
tickets.summary: The mayor's Vision Zero reimagined plan includes over 100 commitments across 19 agencies, with community engagement led mostly by DOT and local officials. The Mayor's Office asked the board to flag any dangerous intersections in the district for inclusion. Action: Identify any problem intersections in the district and send them to the Mayor's Office for inclusion in the Vision Zero plan.

tickets.title: Mobile voting pilot for school council elections
tickets.requester: Health and Human Services committee chair (unnamed); public speakers (unnamed)
tickets.summary: The Health and Human Services committee presented a resolution asking the NYC Department of Education to pilot a mobile voting option for Community Education Council elections, because turnout is about 2% and many households rely only on smartphones. Speakers asked for clear outreach that immigration status is not collected, and for equity in who is elected. Action: Vote on the resolution and send it to the DOE to pilot mobile voting and expand multilingual parent outreach.

tickets.title: NYCHA residents need food and necessities
tickets.summary: A public speaker said NYCHA residents in poverty lack food, water, necessities, and work, and that drugs and toxicity are harming the community. He also said deaf and hard-of-hearing residents need communication access at public meetings and services. Action: Follow up with the district office and relevant agencies on food and necessities access for NYCHA residents and on communication access for deaf residents.

tickets.title: Transit cost support for uptown trips to 125th Street
tickets.summary: A public speaker asked whether transportation costs can be offset, such as through MTA cards or OMNY, for residents who need to travel to the Manhattan Immigrant Welcome Center at 125th Street. He said the trip takes about an hour and requires two or three transfers. Action: Raise the request with the Borough President's office regarding transportation cost support for the uptown welcome center.

tickets.title: East River Pier roller skating rink proposal
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A public speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot multi-use indoor roller skating facility on the East River Pier to replace lost rinks. The proposal includes $8 admission and projects 250 to 500 jobs. Action: Consider the pitch and advise the speaker on the proper land use review process for the East River Pier site.

tickets.title: East River Park stewardship facility procurement delay
tickets.summary: The Parks committee learned the new East River Park facility housing the Lower East Side Ecology Center and stewardship programs is delayed by procurement challenges. The agency offered to return in October with more detail on the delay and interim stewardship support. Action: Ask the agency to return in October with the procurement details, delay timeline, and interim stewardship support plan.

tickets.title: Second vice chair election results
tickets.summary: Two candidates, Daniel Tano and Zachary Thomas, gave speeches for the second vice chair position. Daniel Tano won with 25 votes to Zachary Thomas's 14. Action: None; the election is complete and Daniel Tano was elected second vice chair.

tickets.title: Board trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures
tickets.summary: The board chair announced planned trainings on SLA procedures, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, with dates to be announced. The chair asked members to email topics they want covered. Action: Set dates for the SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures trainings and collect training topic requests by email.

tickets.title: New board member mentor assignment
tickets.summary: The chair welcomed new board member Leila Mahia and said a mentor will be assigned in the near future. Action: Assign a mentor to Leila Mahia.

tickets.title: Bylaws attendance procedure changes
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would address attendance by sending a letter and an executive committee meeting after the first attendance problem, rather than waiting for a longer period. The changes would also remove attendance from the removal process and require public members to follow conflict of interest policies. Action: Vote on the proposed bylaws changes at the October full board meeting, with 28 days' notice sent by email.

tickets.title: Community board budget priorities and district needs vote
tickets.summary: The board will vote in October on district needs and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies, after meeting with over 20 agencies. The district manager noted the draft housing plan has about 7,000 units, with 75% market rate, while affordable housing is the board's top priority. Action: Vote on district needs and ranked budget priorities in each committee and at the October full board.

tickets.title: Draft housing plan comments and ongoing land use engagement
tickets.summary: The city's draft housing plan had a short comment period, so the board commented based on existing positions, and the top comment was that affordable housing must be prioritized. A board member asked whether the land use committee can weigh in on an ongoing basis, and the district manager said shorter comment periods require proactive committee positions. Action: Have committees take proactive positions on housing plans and continue engagement on future drafts.
